name: BattlePlacement_UpdateEntries

score.note: For every active battle owner (BattleParty_PrepareActiveOwners/Func_080b6a60) and every (x in 0..3, y in 0..19) cell, if Func_08077210(owner,x,y) accepts the cell, look up the owner's PlacementTable (owner>7 selects table 1, else table 0 -- identical struct layout to the already-adopted BattlePlacement_UpdateTimedEntries/BattlePlacement_CountValidEntries: PlacementEntry{x,y,id,timer} at PlacementTable+8, count at PlacementTable+264) and, if no existing entry already has that (x,y), register one via Func_080771c8. Then, gated by Func_080770c0(364)==0, walk table 0's entries and clear every permanent entry (timer==-1) whose id has no live battle-object slot (Func_080b7dd0, registered as battle/motion/get_battle_object_slot.c's GetBattleObjectSlot) using the exact same Func_080771b0/Func_080771c0 clear pair BattlePlacement_UpdateTimedEntries uses for expired entries. Byte length matches exactly (306/306); the residual is three independent-instruction-order swaps: the do-while preheader emits the -1 sentinel and the entries-pointer copy in the opposite order from the reference (both instructions present, positions swapped -- the same 'compiler local scheduling mismatch' class already accepted for Func_080b6a60/BattleParty_PrepareActiveOwners), the first Func_080771b0 call's r0/r1 argument-marshalling adds are swapped (values correct, order differs), and the trailing pop{r0}/bx r0 vs pop{r1}/bx r1 epilogue register choice differs. All three are class=allocation, not wrong-instruction; no opcode, operand-value, branch-target, or struct-offset differs anywhere in the function.

rejected_experiments.experiment: s32 owner with plain `owner > 7` (signed compare) for the table selector
rejected_experiments.result: produced ble.n where the reference has bls.n (unsigned) -- fixed by casting only the comparison to (u32)owner > 7, which flipped the branch to bls.n without disturbing anything else

rejected_experiments.experiment: u16 owner (whole-variable unsigned storage) instead of a comparison-site cast
rejected_experiments.result: far worse: 320 candidate bytes vs 306 reference, 155 differing halfwords -- the compiler re-derives owner via a completely different ldrsh/lsls#16/lsrs#16 widening dance and disturbs the count/loop prologue that was otherwise already exact

rejected_experiments.experiment: plain `for` loop with `entry = list->entries` as an initializer before the loop (or as a for-init-clause) for the second (prune) pass
rejected_experiments.result: hoists the entries-pointer setup unconditionally before the count>0 guard (sub sp,#20 + mov r5,sp instead of sub sp,#24 + add r5,sp,#4, plus 14 extra candidate bytes) -- replaced with the explicit guarded do-while idiom already established by BattlePlacement_UpdateTimedEntries's own adopted source, which restored the delayed post-guard setup

rejected_experiments.experiment: direct repeated `entry->id/entry->x/entry->y` field reads as the two calls' arguments (no local caching)
rejected_experiments.result: compiler re-reads memory for every argument of both calls instead of caching id/x/y once and spilling only y across the first call -- caching id/ex/ey into locals once (matching the u8 id = ...; pattern established in BattlePlacement_ResetActiveRuntimeFields/080b5b18) reproduced the reference's single-load-plus-one-spill shape exactly

rejected_experiments.experiment: `list->entries[j].x == x` (field-first) vs `x == list->entries[j].x` (variable-first) in the inner search loop's break condition
rejected_experiments.result: field-first order emitted cmp r3,r6 where the reference has cmp r6,r3 (6 more differing halfwords); variable-first matches exactly

rejected_experiments.experiment: reordering the id/ex/ey local declarations, and nesting the timer==-1 / slot-check condition as two separate ifs instead of &&
rejected_experiments.result: no change or regression on the remaining preheader-order and call-argument-order residual; reverted to the cleaner && form

notes: Below the family-matcher's 7500/10000 adoption threshold (best guess games/gs1/src/battle/placement/update_timed_entries.c at 7349, low confidence) so no automatic transplant workspace existed; recovered by hand-tracing games/gs1/asm/080b5c08.s instruction-by-instruction, cross-checked against the m2c workbench's independent structural reconstruction (which produced the identical control-flow shape, field offsets, and call-argument order from the real agscc type context) and confirmed against three already-adopted or near-adopted siblings: battle/placement/update_timed_entries.c and battle/placement/count_valid_entries.c (identical PlacementEntry/PlacementList/PlacementTable layout and Func_08077000 vocabulary), and battle/motion/get_battle_object_slot.c (Func_080b7dd0's real signature and NULL-return semantics).

Registered the name BattlePlacement_UpdateEntries in games/gs1/source-paths.json and added it as a second .global alias in games/gs1/asm/080b5c08.s (required by check-owners and by the workbench, which resolves the reference symbol through the owner register) -- this is a pre-adoption name registration only; no exact C was adopted, so games/gs1/source-paths.json's entry carries no `source` path and no progress-report refresh is required.

Func_08077210 and Func_080771c8 remain address-named: they are far-call veneers (0x0807a1f9 / 0x0807a459) with no adopted or near-adopted C source anywhere in the repository to draw a real name or full signature from beyond the (s32,s32,s32)->s32/void shape this owner's own assembly and 080ab5e4.c's matching call shape establish.

Recovered only from the retained owner assembly, the approved local en ROM, the approved compiler, already-adopted/near-adopted local sources under games/gs1/src, and the project's own m2c workbench run against the real agscc type context. No other Golden Sun decompilation project, symbol map, or external disassembly was consulted.
